Senses.Explanation: A pronoun rendered 'which one?' in questions and 'that one' when used distally. The expression occurs 2,913 times in 283 allowlisted texts, with the expanded interrogative form occurring 421 times. It drives public interviews by demanding selection or identification: which Mañjuśrī Kāśyapa intended to expel, which eye is the true eye, which is stillness and which illumination, and which is Senior Ming's original face. The same pronoun can contrast with 'this one,' as in Yaoshan's bathing-the-Buddha exchange: 'you can bathe this one; can you also bathe that one?' Another exchange contrasts 'this is the Tathāgata's nirvana' with 'that one is the lecturer's nirvana?' These interrogative and distal constructions are different contextual readings of one deictic pronoun, not different things.
Senses.Note: The expanded interrogative form remains within this corpus-wide sense. Public questions, object demonstrations, person identification, and explicit this/that contrasts establish the deployment range without creating master-specific meanings.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊遂問迦葉。汝擬擯那箇文殊。迦葉無對。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Shakyamuni Buddha biography. Shakyamuni Buddha is the exact speaker who asks Mahakasyapa which Manjusri he intends to expel; Mahakasyapa gives no answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大悲千手眼，那箇是正眼？速道！速道！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Selected Records of the Five Houses (五家語錄（選錄）), Linji Yixuan's encounter with Mayu Baoche. Linji Yixuan is the exact speaker of the stored reply: after Mayu asks which of Great Compassion's thousand hands and eyes is the true eye, Linji repeats the question and commands him to answer quickly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃竪起拂子云：這箇是拂子，且道那箇是寂？那箇是照？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Danxia Zichun (丹霞子淳禪師語錄), hall discourse. Danxia Zichun is the exact speaker who raises the fly-whisk and asks which is stillness and which illumination.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不思善、不思惡，那箇是明上座本來面目？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xishan Liang (西山亮禪師語錄), public case commentary. Huineng is the exact speaker of the stored question asking Huiming which is his original face when not thinking good or evil. Huiming is the named addressee and awakening respondent; Xishan Liang is the later master who raises, interjects on, and finally questions the case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 藥山問。汝祇浴得這箇。還浴得那箇麼。遵云。把將那箇來。藥山便休。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huanglong Huinan (黃龍慧南禪師語錄), bathing-the-Buddha day discourse. Huanglong Huinan is the exact governing speaker who raises and adjudicates the inherited exchange. Inside it, Yaoshan Weiyan asks whether Zun Bunao can bathe 'that one,' and Zun Bunao replies by demanding that 'that one' be brought. Both embedded speakers use the headword; neither replaces Huanglong as the speaker who presents the case to this assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇從汝浴。還浴得那箇麼。遵曰。把將那箇來。師乃休。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Yaoshan Weiyan section. Yaoshan Weiyan is the exact speaker who asks whether Zun Bunao can also bathe 'that one.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖是緣，那箇是佛種？拄杖是一乘法，那箇是緣？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Chengxin Shengzong section. Chengxin Shengzong is the exact hall speaker who raises his staff, calls it the condition, and asks which one is the buddha-seed and which one is the condition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 這箇是如來涅槃，那箇是法師涅槃？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 1–33 (五燈全書(第1卷-第33卷)), Qin Batuo section. Qin Batuo is the exact speaker who rejects the lecturer Sheng's generic definition by saying, 'This one is the Tathagata's nirvana; which one is the scripture lecturer's nirvana?'
